title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I may inform thee that I received a few lines from thee that gave an account of Mary Ward’s illness, of which I was sorry to hear of, so many of the family being poorly. I think it was a fresh trial indeed, & that we had need of our faith and patience to increase as thee express, and not having an opportunity to send a few lines since I heard from thee till now I may inform thee that we are all in reasonable health at present except myself, and may tell thee that I have not been well many days together since Salem meeting. I have had some thoughts of coming to see thee, but the weather is so uncertain at this season of the year & my often being poorly durst not venture. I should be glad if the way was open so as thee could come if not please to write & let me know how you all fare.

closer.salute: So I conclude & remain thy loving & affectionate mother, which my husband joins me in

postscript.p: Please to remember my love to thy Father & mother & little James & Jamie. I had some conversation with Elizabeth Mull and she said that she has often thought that she should like to live with Hannah & if she was at liberty she thought she should make a trial not much prospect of her going at liberty yet the 15th of the 2 mo 1793
